findings.statement:
residual_in_force()'s new ancestry check resolves the tip of the finding-declared accepted_by_audit_branch through _resolve_branch_tip(), which reads `git rev-parse refs/remotes/origin/
^{commit}` FIRST and, on success, never calls ls-remote. refs/remotes/origin/** is a purely local ref namespace writable by any agent with ordinary local git write access via `git update-ref` -- no push, no credentials, no network. Therefore an attacker fabricates a dangling commit containing a forged verdict JSON, fabricates refs/remotes/origin/audit/landing- pointing at it, declares that branch in accepted_by_audit_branch, and the ancestry check passes trivially (the forged commit is its own tip). This is the IDENTICAL threat model to V2-C013's P0.

findings.minimal_remediation:
In _resolve_branch_tip(), invert the order to match [AUDIT_ANCESTRY] lines 489-495: (1) `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/
` as the FIRST and ONLY tip source, die immediately if the branch is absent on origin; (2) `git fetch origin refs/heads/

Also correct the docstring / die message / ledger machine_check wording ('실시간 tip', '같은 원천·순서', '원격 브랜치 tip') to match what the code actually does.

findings.statement: abrr_grant_hits() replaced the previous strict TOP-LEVEL 3-way equality (adj['id']==fid and verdict=='ACCEPT_RECLASSIFY' and new_class==ABRR) with a full-document recursive scan. This is strictly a LOOSENING: any object at any depth whose id/verdict/new_class match now counts as a grant, and accepted_by_audit_report is attacker-chosen, so any JSON file readable at the declared sha is a candidate. The negation vocabulary (_ABRR_ADJ_NEGATE) inspects only verdict and new_class of the same object -- sibling annotations such as {"outcome":"blocked"} or {"fabricated":true} do not neutralize a hit.
findings.currently_exploitable: NO (measured). Recursively scanned every research/landing_accessibility/**.json in the tree of origin/audit/landing-adversarial's tip for grant-shaped objects (ACCEPT_RECLASSIFY and new_class==ABRR and no negation vocabulary): exactly 1 hit, and it is the legitimate top-level adjudication in V2_C008_focused.json.
findings.why_it_matters: Self-inflicted footgun: the moment an adversarial auditor records an attack payload in a report as a JSON OBJECT rather than a string, that report itself becomes live grant evidence. My own V2_C013.json was safe only incidentally -- it stored the forged payload as a string (fake_commit_content). _ABRR_CANON (L-2) still gates which ids can be granted, so this alone cannot mint a new acceptance. control's still_not_blocked.L-7 discloses only the nesting-order residual, not this angle.
findings.minimal_remediation: Restrict recursive hits to the top-level object or to an allowlist of container keys (condition_adjudications / prior_findings_status / findings), or widen the negation check to the serialized form of the whole matched object.
